title: Everyday Materials (KS1)
subject: Science
strapline: What things are made of and how we describe them.
facts: Common materials include wood, plastic, glass, metal, water, rock, paper and fabric.
An object is the thing; the material is what it is made from — a spoon (object) can be made of metal (material).
We describe materials with property words: hard, soft, bendy, stiff, shiny, dull, rough, smooth, waterproof.
The same object can be made from different materials — a cup can be plastic, glass or paper.
We choose a material to suit the job: glass is see-through, so it is good for windows.
Some materials are transparent (you can see through them), some are opaque (you cannot).
You can change the shape of some materials by squashing, bending, twisting or stretching them.

quick_quiz.q: What material is best for a window because you can see through it?
Give a property word for a rock.
A spoon is the object. What might the material be?

teacher_tips: Sort a tray of real objects by material, then by a property (bendy vs stiff).
Keep "object" and "material" separate — a common mix-up.
Ask "why is it made of that?" to link property to purpose.
